morph_3d/morph_sdf_raymarching.description: Blend analytic distance fields without extracting a triangle surface.
walkthrough: SDFEntity3D wraps sphere, torus and box distance definitions. The raymarch strategy evaluates the blended field along view rays instead of interpolating matching endpoint vertices.
Bounding padding must contain the visible field. Material changes affect shading, while distance definitions and morph weight determine the intermediate silhouette.
experiments: Reduce an endpoint radius and inspect the intermediate field from several angles. Keep raymarch settings fixed.

morph_3d/morph_sdf_volumetric.description: Extract a changing isosurface while morphing spatial primitives.
walkthrough: The volumetric strategy samples endpoint representations and reconstructs a triangle surface with marching cubes. This differs from rendering an analytic field directly with raymarching.
Resolution affects reconstruction detail and GPU workload. Metallic materials make normal changes conspicuous but do not themselves create the morph.
experiments: Lower the configured grid resolution and compare the torus hole during transition. Keep roughness unchanged.

morph_3d/morph_superquadric.description: Compare a sphere, rounded cube, cylinder, diamond and pillow through exponent changes.
walkthrough: Signed powers of sine and cosine define the superquadric parameterization. Two exponents control the cross-section in different directions.
Each stage shares sampling structure, allowing corresponding points to blend. Normal calculations require guards near degenerate values and affect shading independently of position.
experiments: Change only one exponent in the pillow stage. Compare horizontal and vertical curvature.

morph_3d/morph_swarm_trajectories.description: Compare several particle flight paths between mesh targets.
walkthrough: The swarm strategy uses particles to bridge target shapes. The trajectory configuration selects spiral, fluid, scatter or linear movement rather than changing the target mesh.
The scene repeats transitions with different configurations and updates its badge. Keep particle count and duration steady when judging trajectory differences.
experiments: Use the same target pair and duration for linear and spiral modes. Follow one region of particles rather than the whole silhouette.

morph_3d/morph_swarm.description: Form and dissolve mesh silhouettes with a GPU particle swarm.
walkthrough: Torus, sphere and cube provide target geometry. The swarm configuration controls particle sampling, motion and appearance between those targets.
Curl-like motion adds intermediate turbulence; it is distinct from the final target correspondence. Large particle counts increase workload even though geometry is shared.
experiments: Reduce particle count before changing turbulence strength. Compare target readability with the amount of intermediate scatter.

morph_3d/morph_torus_family.description: Follow a torus as its hole closes and its parameterization becomes singular.
walkthrough: Major and minor radii select ring, horn and spindle tori. ParametricModel supplies corresponding samples through the stages.

When major radius reaches minor radius, the hole pinches at a singular point; spindle stages can self-intersect. The near-sphere endpoint is a limiting parameterization, not a nonsingular topology-preserving deformation.
experiments: Stop at equal major and minor radii and orbit around the pinch. Compare that stage with a slightly larger major radius.

morph_3d/swarm_morph.description: Drive a particle-based MorphModel with an explicit weight animation.
walkthrough: The endpoint sphere and cube supply sample targets. MorphModel owns the swarm representation, and CustomAnimation changes its weight.
The model rotates while the weight progresses forward and back. Camera movement changes the view independently of both swarm motion and model rotation.
experiments: Hold weight at 0.5 and disable model rotation. Inspect particle distribution before changing swarm settings.

multi_pass/compute_sim.description: Render values written by an earlier compute pass.
walkthrough: A CustomComputePass writes a storage buffer, and Shader reads that buffer to color a screen quad. The time uniform controls the generated values.
Pass ordering must make the compute result available before its consumer renders. The torus is ordinary scene geometry sharing the final composition.
experiments: Replace the compute formula with a constant. Confirm the background freezes while the torus keeps rotating.

multi_pass/multipass.description: Generate a background, render the scene, then apply a CRT filter.
walkthrough: The compute pass creates wave data; the background Shader consumes it. A spatial torus joins that background during scene rendering.
PostProcessPass reads the renderer’s final output and applies channel offsets, scanlines and a vignette. Its input is the composed image rather than the original storage buffer.
experiments: Remove the final CRT pass and compare the same scene. Then alter the compute formula to isolate an earlier pipeline stage.

multi_pass/multipass2.description: Apply edge detection and RGB splitting to a compute-driven scene.
walkthrough: A compute pass generates plasma values that the background shader maps to color. A box and wireframe sphere add spatial content.
The active postprocess is a Sobel-style edge treatment with channel splitting, rather than the Gaussian blur suggested by the old registry description. It processes the rendered image as a whole.
experiments: Disable RGB offsets while retaining edge detection. Compare edge emphasis with chromatic displacement.

multi_pass/outline_showcase.description: Install an outline pass around moving spatial objects.
walkthrough: OutlinePlugin integrates the pass through scene.use. The floor, cubes and sphere render normally before the outline treatment reads scene information.
Thickness controls the visible edge treatment; model rotation changes which contours are exposed. Material color remains separate from the outline.
experiments: Change thickness from 1.5 to 0.5 and inspect the sphere silhouette and cube creases.

multi_pass/vhsc_showcase.description: Add a CRT-style image treatment after rendering a rotating cube.
walkthrough: The cube is ordinary Model geometry. PostProcessPass consumes the final scene texture and samples separate red, green and blue offsets.
Scanlines and vignette modify the same image after scene rendering. They do not alter mesh topology or lighting inputs.
experiments: Set all RGB sampling offsets to zero while retaining scanlines. Compare channel separation with the remaining treatment.

new_shader_architecture/3d_line.description: Generate two spatial line strands directly in GPU buffers.
walkthrough: Each point buffer stores four floats per point. A compute dispatch writes strand positions from time and a phase offset; Line3D consumes those buffers.
refreshLength updates derived line information after computation. Stroke shader and overlap prevention affect rendering independently of the strand geometry.
experiments: Change the second strand’s phase offset from pi to pi/2. Compare separation while keeping stroke width fixed.

new_shader_architecture/cloth_sim.description: Animate a mesh with analytic waves computed on the GPU.
walkthrough: The CPU creates grid topology, then a compute shader updates vertex heights and analytic normals. Model consumes the same GPU vertex and index buffers.
Despite the file name, the active kernel does not integrate masses and springs. Its surface motion is prescribed by sine and cosine formulas.
experiments: Set the secondary-wave amplitude to zero. Compare the radial wave and its normals with the combined surface.

new_shader_architecture/mesh2d.description: Displace a triangulated two-dimensional grid through a compute shader.
walkthrough: CPU arrays define initial vertices and triangle indices. STORAGE and VERTEX buffer usage lets the compute kernel write data that Mesh2D renders.
Each frame uploads time, dispatches computation and submits commands before rendering. Buffer layout must agree across CPU packing, WGSL and the mesh renderer.
experiments: Reduce the grid resolution and increase displacement amplitude. Inspect triangle edges and overall deformation separately.

new_shader_architecture/path_compute.description: Write a changing contour into a GPU buffer and render it as a path.
walkthrough: ComputeKernel receives point storage and a parameter uniform. Path consumes the resulting point buffer instead of reparsing an SVG string every frame.
The kernel dispatch changes geometry; stroke color and glow change appearance. Refreshing derived path data keeps rendering consistent with the new points.
experiments: Freeze time uploaded to the kernel while retaining stroke-color updates. Compare a static contour with changing paint.

new_shader_architecture/path.description: Render an SVG contour through the vector-path pipeline.
walkthrough: Path parses the supplied SVG data into contours. Its stroke settings determine how those contours appear without introducing a separate animation.
CameraController allows inspection of the static result. This is a baseline for comparing CPU-authored path data with GPU-buffer-driven paths.
experiments: Change only strokeWidth, then alter one SVG control point. Compare paint thickness with geometric curvature.

new_shader_architecture/poly_showcase.description: Build a closed star polygon and reveal its custom-shaded outline.
walkthrough: The source alternates radii while generating Vec2 points. Poly closes the contour and uses separate fill and stroke treatments.
The stroke shader controls color along the contour, while CustomAnimation changes reveal progress. A visible stroke color is still needed to activate the stroke pass.
experiments: Change the inner radius without changing the shader. Compare the star silhouette with its unchanged stroke pattern.

new_shader_architecture/rotating_triangl.description: Generate triangle vertices with a minimal compute pipeline.
walkthrough: A storage/vertex buffer holds three two-component points. The compute shader rotates their coordinates from a time uniform before Triangle renders them.
The source submits the compute command directly each update. Uniform allocation and bind-group layout must match WGSL even for this small example.
experiments: Freeze the uploaded time, then change the triangle fill. Compare stationary GPU geometry with a paint-only edit.

new_shader_architecture/sprite.description: Compare image, video, canvas and GPU-deformed sprite sources.
walkthrough: The four panels share Sprite rendering but receive different sources. An OffscreenCanvas updates its pixels, while the compute panel changes its vertex positions.
Pixel refresh and geometry deformation are separate operations. Browser media policy may require interaction before the video plays with audio.
experiments: Stop canvas refresh while leaving its drawing code active. Compare stale pixels with the independently moving compute sprite.

new_shader_architecture/text_showcase.description: Compare vector text, distance-field text and LaTeX geometry.
walkthrough: Text provides glyph paths, SDFText provides atlas-based typography, and Tex converts a mathematical expression. The staged sequence exposes outlines, fills and scale changes.
Vector reveal progress differs from scaling distance-field glyphs. Font and typesetting resources must load before their respective text can appear.
experiments: Apply the same scale animation to Text and SDFText. Inspect edge quality and the difference in available contour-reveal behavior.

new_shader_architecture/write_animation.description: Draw vector text and a typeset equation in sequence.
walkthrough: Text constructs ordinary glyph paths; Tex constructs equation paths. Write progressively introduces those existing contours.
The awaited play calls make the equation follow the sentence. Duration controls drawing time rather than typesetting complexity.
experiments: Run the two Write animations in one play call. Compare simultaneous drawing with the original ordered introduction.
